source_context: While investigating OEIS A053067, GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT derived and formalized an unconditional Euclid-type residue theorem. For every nonzero modulus m and every lower bound B, the submission constructs n > B and a decimal width d such that the entire triangular block defining A053067(n) lies in the d-digit interval and its fixed-width decimal concatenation is congruent to 1 modulo m. The proof decomposes m into its 2/5-supported and prime-to-10 parts, uses absorption by powers of 10 on the former, Euler-period congruences on the latter, and explicit quantitative bounds to keep the constructed triangular block inside one decimal width. This does not prove another prime term exists; it proves that no finite modular obstruction can cover the sequence.
